units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

The source's stated purpose of avoiding distraction does not introduce a separate requirement to prove actual investor distraction. The marketing claim's missing-paragraph uncertainty is stale: db43e253bea18.u3.792 supplies the services context, and db43e253bea18.u20.5257 through db43e253bea18.u22.6374 supply the marketing provisions. Their presence resolves that evidential gap without making advertising truthfulness a condition of the gift restriction.

Scope placement changes outcomes under the declared runtime semantics. node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e places offering in scope; node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 place promotional conditions in scope. Known absence returns OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed question's not-caught or satisfies-control Boolean. An intentional assessment-domain restriction and a question-correspondence mismatch remain competing explanations.

Unknown scope also prevents operational equivalence. With a known distributor, unknown offering and a component known not to be a gift, node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns UNKNOWN, whereas the corresponding result-level conjunction in node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b returns FALSE, assuming no conflicting facts. Analogous differences occur when promotional scope is unknown but a discount or non-gift classification is known.

The two offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift classification. Their stated facts do not expressly bind that connection to the same gift component. In a mixed offer, this can impose an unsupported prohibition if the qualifying gift is unrelated to the promoted product. The aggregation can be sufficient if the supplied judgments establish that the promotional connection covers that gift; that condition is not explicit.

node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 uses provider for the regulated actor. If this denotes the distributor making the offer, the terminology adds no condition. If it requires funding or fulfilment by that distributor, it can exclude an otherwise caught offered gift without source support. node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b expressly distinguishes offer attribution from funding and fulfilment.

db43e253bea18.u0.2 defines distributors in the circular's SFC-authorised-fund context, while db43e253bea18.u13.2987 states the gift rule in investment-product terms. Fund-specific scope is supported for this circular; the packet does not establish the complete reach of paragraph 3.11 outside that context.

db43e253bea18.u12.2646 says returns or incentives may be considered gifts. Incentive or guaranteed-return status alone therefore does not establish gift classification. db43e253bea18.u7.1360 also distinguishes fund return from distributor top-up. The candidates leave substantive classification to supplied judgments; their formulas do not perform that assessment.

The aggregate fact in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 is less explicit about evidence completeness than the aggregate in node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5. A FALSE existential classification requires sufficient evidence that no relevant offered component qualifies. An incomplete component inventory or unresolved classification does not by itself establish FALSE.

The circular states a purpose of avoiding distraction, not a separate prerequisite of proven actual distraction. Its quoted gift rule does not require actual payment, receipt, acceptance or an invitation to the public. Adding any of those prerequisites would create an unsupported permission to offer an otherwise caught gift. Conversely, truthful advertising or section 103 authorisation is not stated to excuse the gift restriction.

The component candidates are not operationally equivalent under the declared runtime semantics. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b place only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also places the offer occurrence in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f places the combined offer-and-promotion fact in scope. A known absence of an offer or promotional link can therefore produce FALSE in one candidate and OUT_OF_SCOPE in another. Unknown scope can also prevent a known non-gift or discount fact from determining the result. The intended question domain must resolve these alternatives.

Both offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift fact. Unless the supplied classifications bind the promotional connection to the same offered component, they may catch an unrelated gift merely because another part of the offer promotes a product. The source connects the gifts themselves to the relevant promotion. Component-linked assessment and aggregation require explicit attribution.

The source says additional returns or incentives may be considered gifts; it does not classify every guaranteed return or incentive automatically. The circular defines distributors through distribution of SFC-authorised funds, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 refers to investment products generally. The component exception must concern the assessed component itself. A discount elsewhere in a combined offer cannot establish the exception for a separate gift. FALSE for a prohibition question, TRUE for node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5's selected-control compliance question, and OUT_OF_SCOPE are not general legal permissions. Separate advertising, structured-product and other duties may remain applicable.

Scope placement changes observable answers even among candidates with the same question hash. For a known distributor and a known unoffered component, node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b can return FALSE, while node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE. Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f also places the offered-and-linked condition in scope. These are not runtime-equivalent alternatives; the intended distinction between not caught and out of scope needs resolution.

Scope differences also affect incomplete evidence. Under the declared runtime semantics, an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN even where a known non-gift or qualifying discount would make a corresponding unscoped prohibition conjunction FALSE. This is an executable distinction, not evidence that the circular imposes an additional legal restriction.

The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine offer-level promotional linkage with existence of a non-discount gift component. The source says, "If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product". Unless the fact contract establishes that the identified gift participates in the linked promotion, the formula can combine a product-linked component with a different, unlinked gift and overstate the restriction. Whether an offer-wide link suffices remains unresolved.

The offer-level existential facts require complete enough component evidence to support FALSE. Node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 expressly states, "False requires sufficient evidence that no offered component meets both conditions; unresolved classification remains unknown." Node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not expressly state this completeness condition. Its generic UNKNOWN semantics do not themselves implement component enumeration or prevent an incorrectly supplied FALSE.

A fee or charge discount is an exception to the selected gift restriction, not a general permission under the circular. Likewise, node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5's TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT result is confined to the selected gift control. Reading either as overall legality would omit the independently supported advertising and section 103 duties.

The source states that guaranteed returns or other incentives "may be considered a gift" in db43e253bea18.u12.2646. Their classification must remain individual and unresolved where evidence is insufficient. The representations generally preserve this qualification; no automatic gift classification or blanket permission for guaranteed returns follows from these checks.

Node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b distinguishes the offeror from whoever funds or fulfils a benefit. The source's wording "distributors should not offer any gifts" supports focusing on offering rather than receipt. However, it does not independently resolve disputed attribution, agency or third-party arrangements. Those remain classification questions, not implemented conclusions.

The circular defines distributors by reference to intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 uses the broader words "a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product". Fund-specific candidate definitions can fit this circular's selected scope, but their equivalence to the full Code provision outside that scope is not established.

The supplied units do not establish an effective interval for the candidates' stated temporal basis. The explicit date 30 September 2010 identifies the FAQ cited in footnote 3; it is not an effective date for every rule or dependency. Applicable versions and competing temporal interpretations remain unresolved.

The declared global CONFLICT blocking and UNKNOWN propagation are supplied runtime conventions, not requirements derived from the circular. They preserve uncertainty but should not be described as legal prohibitions or permissions.

With distributor status true, offering false and no conflicts, the former return FALSE and the latter OUT_OF_SCOPE. node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f similarly places the combined offering/promotion fact in scope. These distinctions require an explicit interface decision; FALSE and OUT_OF_SCOPE must not be treated as interchangeable.

Unknown scope can prevent a determinate result that result-level conjunction would otherwise permit. For example, a known discount cannot resolve UNKNOWN promotional scope in node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f, whereas a false non-discount condition can determine FALSE in a result-level conjunction. These are executable differences, not evidence that the circular prescribes either uncertainty policy.

The offer-level candidates separate the offer's promotional link from the existence of a non-discount gift component. They could overcapture an unrelated gift bundled with a product promotion unless the supplied classifications establish that the same component is offered in the qualifying promotion. Neither aggregation predicate explicitly checks that connection for its existential witness.

The gift candidates depend on supplied substantive classifications. Their formulas do not establish distributor status, gift status, discount status or the promotional link. Paragraph 9 supports preserving uncertainty about incentives and guaranteed returns; it does not establish that every additional return is a gift or that every non-structured-product arrangement is permitted.

node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b states that offer attribution is independent of funding or fulfilment. The circular's focus on offering supports not requiring completed payment or receipt, but it does not fully resolve every third-party funding, fulfilment or attribution arrangement. That broader classification assertion remains unverified.

The circular defines distributors by reference to intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2. Some candidate definitions expressly retain that limitation and others use broader distributor language. Conversely, paragraph 10 speaks of a specific investment product or particular product type. Whether these definitions coincide within the retained source scope must be established before treating the candidates as equivalent.

The gift-control authorities are not independently supplied: paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct and the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010, identified in footnotes 2 and 3. Their absence does not erase the circular's express gift rule, but prevents verification of additional definitions, qualifications or interpretive conditions against those external texts. No dependency IDs can be assigned.

The broader advertising authorities are also absent: paragraph 2.3 of the Code of Conduct, the SFC’s Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes, and the FAQs and other guidance referenced by footnote 4. NONE_DECLARED in the advertising checks applies only to the explicit extracted duties, not to independent verification of all incorporated advertising requirements.

The candidates state 'stated source interval; competing date/time interpretations retained', but the packet supplies no concrete applicability interval or competing date interpretations. Temporal availability and the applicable versions of external authorities remain unverified.

The three structured-product disputes remain marked unresolved in the supplied prior evidence, without identified disagreeing dimensions. The present proposals separate direct support for the circular's qualified statement from missing authority for independent statutory verification. If authority assessment is confined strictly to extraction, NONE_DECLARED is the narrower alternative; MISSING here identifies the additional statute required for independent classification, not a failure of source support.

A false combined offering/promotion fact similarly places node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f outside scope. Whether these exclusions are intended domain restrictions or incomplete answers to the stated false_means remains unresolved.

Unknown promotional scope can prevent a determinate result even when a known discount would defeat prohibition in a result-level conjunction. The shared global conflict rule can likewise block a result despite a decisive Boolean condition. These are declared runtime policies, not uncertainty rules established by the circular.

The offer-level candidates place promotional linkage at offer level and gift classification in a separate existential predicate. Unless supplied facts connect the same gift component to the qualifying promotion, an unrelated gift bundled with a product promotion could produce an unsupported prohibition. Conversely, assuming the entire offer establishes that connection requires explicit justification.

The circular defines distributors through intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds, while paragraph 10 uses specific investment products and product types. The candidates vary between broader distributor wording and express SFC-authorised-fund limitations. Their actor and product scopes are not established as equivalent.

Gift status remains a supplied substantive judgment. Paragraph 9 says guaranteed returns and other incentives may be gifts; it does not classify them automatically. Paragraph 5 distinguishes fund return from distributor top-up. Neither structured-product status nor its absence settles the gift classification of either component.

The focus on offering supports not requiring completed payment or receipt. However, node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b's statements about funding, fulfilment and attribution do not establish how every third-party arrangement should be classified. Those attribution questions remain unverified rather than automatically constituting executable defects.

Independent verification of the gift standard requires missing external materials: paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct and the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010, identified by footnotes 2 and 3. Can their applicable versions be supplied? No supplied dependency IDs identify them.

Independent verification of the broader advertising regime requires missing Code of Conduct paragraph 2.3, the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes, and the supplementary FAQs and guidance referenced in footnote 4. Can their applicable versions be supplied? NONE_DECLARED in the advertising checks concerns only the circular's explicit narrow duties.

The advertising antecedent is anchored by paragraph 3 and the preceding marketing discussion. Application to a particular service still requires factual classification. The deposit-parallel claim captures one express duty, not every adjacent restriction concerning deposit-like arrangements, deposit-rate comparisons or savings representations.

The packet supplies no concrete applicability interval or competing date interpretations. The candidates' temporal-basis wording does not establish the applicable assessment date or versions of external authorities.

A TRUE gift-compliance result or FALSE gift-prohibition result establishes no general permission and no compliance with section 103, advertising, disclosure or redemption requirements. Separate statutory and advertising duties must likewise not be inserted as additional gift-prohibition conditions.

The disclosure claim's statement that footnote 1 is not supplied is incorrect for this packet: db43e253bea18.u27.7511 supplies it. The claim captures the absence-of-guarantees disclosure, but the source also requires disclosure that investors may not recover principal. That additional duty should remain separately represented if the disclosure regime is modeled.

The advertising claim is supported within the services context developed in db43e253bea18.u3.792 and db43e253bea18.u20.5257–u22.6374. Extending it to every advertisement or treating every reference to savings as a gift would exceed the supplied claim and source context.

External texts absent from the packet include Handbook Overarching Principles section 6.4; Code of Conduct paragraphs 2.3 and 3.11; the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQ issued on 30 September 2010; and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes with their supplementary FAQs and guidance. No supplied dependency IDs identify these texts. They are not necessary to establish the two narrow claims expressly stated in the circular, so the pair assessments use NONE_DECLARED. Their absence prevents independent verification of broader interpretations, exceptions or subsequent changes.

Candidates sharing the component question are not operationally equivalent. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b place only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also places offering in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f also places linked promotion in scope. With a known distributor and a known absence of an offer, the former two can return FALSE while the latter two return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this alternative rather than treating the shared question hash as proof of equivalence.

Scope placement also changes uncertainty behavior. A false non-scope gift predicate can resolve a conjunction to FALSE despite an unknown offer or promotional link, whereas an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN before the result is evaluated. The intended boundary between applicability and a negative answer requires an explicit decision; the source does not specify these runtime states.

The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine offer-level promotional linkage with the existence of a non-discount gift component. Their facts do not expressly require that the same component be offered in the linked promotion. In a mixed offer, the definitions need to establish that connection or retain uncertainty; otherwise unrelated components could be combined to produce an unsupported prohibition.

node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 uses 'provider' for the actor, while node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b expressly attributes the offer to an offeror independently of funding or fulfilment. The source regulates distributors who offer gifts. A provider interpreted only as the funder or fulfiller could identify the wrong actor. Conversely, the supplied passage does not settle every agency or third-party attribution question.

The source says guaranteed returns and other incentives 'may be considered a gift'. Automatic classification of every return, top-up or incentive as a gift would add an unsupported restriction. The component candidates preserve classification as a supplied judgment; the shorter offer-level definition in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 should not be populated through an automatic incentive-to-gift assumption.

The fee-or-charge discount exception concerns the assessed component. A separate discount cannot exempt another gift component. Conversely, failing the gift restriction is not established merely because a benefit is not a discount: gift classification and the requisite offer and promotional relationship remain necessary.

The SFC-authorised-fund limitation is supported as the circular's setting by db43e253bea18.u0.2, while paragraph 3.11 is quoted using the broader term 'investment product'. Narrow fund-specific candidates may fit the selected circular scope; they should not be presented as complete implementations of paragraph 3.11 for all investment products without resolving that scope distinction.

TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT in node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 means satisfaction of the selected gift control only. FALSE in a prohibition candidate and OUT_OF_SCOPE likewise provide no general permission. Offering-document disclosure, misleading-advertising duties and section 103 may remain independently applicable.

The supplied representations declare temporal and conflict-handling semantics, but the packet does not establish concrete operative intervals or provide an executed implementation. These checks assess the quoted expressions only; they do not validate runtime behavior, settle competing temporal interpretations or establish current-law applicability.

The XML statement is supported as a listed-method permission; an alternative reading that treats its extracted conditions as exhaustive sufficient conditions is contradicted by the omitted e-Cert requirement.

The separately provided JFIU XML schema is absent. The circular establishes the obligation to follow it, but not its contents. None of the four opaque dependency IDs identifies that schema, and none has a non-null source_hash; no AVAILABLE assessment or invented dependency mapping is justified.

Both compliance candidates expressly exclude XML-schema conformity from their XML facts. Their TRUE results must remain limited to the selected channel, method and e-Cert control. They do not establish full XML compliance or satisfaction of the separate obligation to liaise with JFIU to arrange a technical test. The source does not expressly make successful completion of that test a precondition to each filing.

Footnote 3 requires a Hongkong Post e-Cert without specifying its operational use. The submission-specific supplied-or-used requirement in node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 may implement that requirement, but the packet does not establish the added operational interpretation or establish that possession alone is insufficient. What JFIU instructions define satisfaction of the e-Cert requirement? Those instructions are missing and have no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The prescribed PDF form is missing external material needed to assess the completed-prescribed-PDF classifications. Which prescribed form or specification governs the submission, and which dependency ID identifies it? No supplied mapping resolves this.

The date-only trigger in node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes the portion of 2 February 2026 before 9:00am. The source separately gives a date-effective channel rule, a 9:00am operational launch and resubmission following implementation. The calendar-date and operational-launch interpretations remain distinct; the date-only predicate cannot distinguish that morning's blackout from the launch.

The timestamp candidates choose an inclusive operational-launch boundary. The packet does not expressly state the governing timezone or definitively resolve how the date-effective provision relates to 'following its implementation' at the exact launch instant. What authoritative clarification resolves these temporal classifications? No supplied dependency ID identifies such clarification.

The blackout provision directs urgent filers to contact JFIU. Contact alone does not establish submission of an STR, but an actual submission resulting from that contact must be assessed on its evidence. Do not generalize post-launch channel exclusivity into the blackout or treat migration as a new original submission.

Non-filing events return FALSE in node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb when its licensed-firm scope holds and facts are nonconflicting, whereas the other event candidates place actual filing in scope and return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this domain distinction instead of treating the candidates as equivalent.

The history candidate answers whether a qualifying event existed, not whether a duty remains outstanding after later resubmission. Its existential assessment is supplied externally; the formula does not inspect history. FALSE needs enough historical evidence to exclude qualifying events.

The circular promises JFIU resubmission guidance, but that guidance is absent. Which guidance governs performance of the resubmission duty, and which dependency ID identifies it? Its absence does not erase the expressly stated trigger or make unrelated method permissions relevant to that trigger.

Rule-wide conflict blocking can prevent evaluation even when an alternative method would otherwise suffice. This is a declared runtime policy, not an additional substantive restriction established by the circular. Missing classifications, conflicts and unresolved temporal facts must retain their declared non-Boolean outcomes.

Footnote 3 has anchors in both da12aecad4e68.u4.1003 and da12aecad4e68.u5.1078. The extraction's absent-anchor uncertainty is resolved. Extending the e-Cert requirement to every submission method or every resubmission is unsupported. Absence of an anchor on the web-form option also does not establish an exemption from requirements outside this packet.

Registration, XML-schema conformity and e-Cert use are not stated prerequisites to the resubmission trigger. Adding them as necessary trigger operands would impose unsupported restrictions. Omitting them from these trigger formulas does not establish overall submission compliance.

Node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses "[the fact filing_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2026-02-02]", which includes filings before 9:00am that day. The source separately says "With effect from 2 February 2026" in da12aecad4e68.u3.811 and "upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026" in da12aecad4e68.u13.2131. The calendar-date and operational-launch readings of "following its implementation" remain distinct; these pair assessments do not settle that disagreement.

The operational-launch candidates use an inclusive 9:00am boundary. The source supports a 9:00am launch but does not expressly state the governing timezone or resolve exact-boundary inclusion in the resubmission provision. What authoritative JFIU clarification or applicable time convention resolves those points? Any necessary additional authority is absent and has no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The blackout provision in da12aecad4e68.u12.1941 directs urgent submitters to contact JFIU. It does not establish that every email, telephone call or fax constitutes an actual STR submission, nor grant a general post-launch alternative-channel permission. Automatic migration under da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 likewise does not itself establish a new submission event.

Actual STR filing appears in the scope of nodes node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098, node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913 and node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1. Node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb instead puts submission in its result. A licensed actor's nonfiling event can therefore produce OUT_OF_SCOPE versus FALSE. Equivalence requires an established assessment domain that excludes such events.

Node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3 delegates event existence, temporal interpretation, channel classification and sufficient-history assessment to a supplied Boolean. Its executable result is "Result: the fact report_has_postlaunch_other_channel_submission"; the formula does not perform an existential search. Incomplete history without an observed qualifying event must not be treated as an established FALSE. Attribution to the report's responsible entity also requires care when different entities made different submissions.

These typed questions concern historical DUTY_TRIGGER results. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission does not erase an earlier triggering event, while historical TRUE does not establish that the resulting duty remains outstanding. "Declared output convention: TRUE_IS_SATISFIED" must retain the typed meaning of trigger existence rather than compliance.

The XML provision also requires firms to liaise with JFIU as soon as possible to arrange a technical test. The schema claim is supported as an atomic extraction but does not exhaust da12aecad4e68.u14.2439. This additional action remains separate from the trigger questions.

JFIU's promised resubmission guidance in da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 is absent and has no identifiable supplied dependency mapping. Can the guidance and its applicable version be supplied for any assessment of performance or discharge? The source does not make issuance of that guidance a prerequisite to the stated duty.

All four supplied external dependencies have null source_hash values and no identifying metadata. None qualifies as AVAILABLE or can safely be matched to the XML schema, resubmission guidance or timezone authority. Source unit IDs are evidence identifiers, not external dependency IDs.

The declared UNKNOWN, CONFLICT and scope semantics are distinct from the legal trigger conditions. In particular, a conflicting dependency blocks evaluation even if another operand would otherwise determine the Boolean result. These scoped claim checks do not independently validate that runtime policy.

witness_requirements: The parent retains separate conditions that the assessed event is an actual STR submission and that evidence from separate attempts is not combined; the children do not execute or preserve the event-level evidence-separation condition.

The parent limits footnote 3 to the XML and prescribed-PDF alternatives; the children leave this as an unresolved source-boundary issue, so the executable relation does not preserve that scope condition.

The parent separately excludes XML-schema conformity, technical testing, reporting timeliness, substantive STR adequacy, and overall legal compliance from the selected decision; those limitations are omitted from the executable children.

The parent retains blackout urgent-contact and post-implementation resubmission distinctions, including that resubmission does not alter the original event’s channel or time; the children do not execute these conditions.

The parent states that no event-level truth value is assigned because the certificate relationship is unresolved. The child statement preserves that unresolved issue, but the resulting child set cannot evaluate the broader parent proposition with all of its stated conditions.

No executable preservation is demonstrated: the sole child has null formalization and is UNENCODED with E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE. Actor, filing-event scope, temporal scope, method alternatives, certificate attachment and unknown-value handling survive only in prose.
The parent expression uses undeclared is_xml_submission. Neither that defect nor the missing XML schema is resolved by the proposal.
The certificate requirement remains attached only to XML and prescribed PDF, without an added web-form requirement; its operational satisfaction conditions remain unspecified.
Equating implementation with the inclusive 9:00am launch boundary remains an interpretation. The date-level effective provision and the unspecified timezone are not conclusively resolved.

Blackout urgent contact and mandatory resubmission after an off-channel filing remain prose residuals, not executable obligations. A later compliant filing cannot by itself establish discharge of a particular earlier filing's resubmission duty.
The XML technical-test liaison duty is outside the selected filing control in both versions; neither version establishes compliance with that separate source obligation.
The children narrow the actor from the parent’s general STR context to licensed firms, matching the cited SFC circular but adding a scope condition not explicit in the parent statement.

The contact child restates the blackout with exact intraday boundaries and frames the trigger as each STR requiring urgent submission; the source does not define urgency or establish that contact completes filing.

The history child adds the separate express re-submission obligation for post-implementation submissions through other channels. This is properly bounded and does not assert that blackout contact itself is a submission, but it adds a conditional rule beyond the parent’s original wording.

The executable bundle adds valid_from = 2026-09-26, after the entire blackout. Preservation requires an explicit distinction between bundle-version validity and the historical instant being assessed; none is supplied.

Urgency is tested at the assessed instant, while contact may occur anywhere during the blackout. The executable does not establish that credited contact occurred by that instant or addressed the urgency being assessed.
The test covers one firm and one STR. Its Boolean result cannot establish performance for all qualifying STRs.
Urgency classification and completion of urgent reporting remain unresolved; r2_completion is explicitly unencoded.
Schema conformity and liaison as soon as possible remain mandatory but unencoded: the performance child returned E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE.
The executable result determines current trigger satisfaction only; it does not determine compliance or discharge of previously triggered duties.
The bundle's valid_from date of 26 September 2026 is not a source-derived commencement date and does not establish coverage of earlier transition assessments.
The executable child formalizes only the trigger; the mandatory performance duty remains unencoded, so complete parent satisfaction cannot be computed.
The proposal retains the source's unspecified resubmission timing and linkage requirements as explicit residual questions.

The proposal adds an evidentiary requirement for time-of-day classification of implementation, which is a stated interpretation of the 9:00am launch boundary rather than a substantive change to the duty.

All three actual executable children are UNENCODED: the interval and follow-up children report E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE, and the contact child reports E_SCHEMA. Executable preservation is therefore unestablished.
The proposed Boolean urgency fact does not encode the exact clock-time interval or link an urgent submission event to that interval.
The proposed contact fact does not explicitly bind the contact to the same STR, its urgency, or the blackout interval; unrelated historical contact could satisfy an inadequately grounded valuation.
The licensed-firm actor, every applicable STR, direct contact, and specified contact destinations remain prose conditions without demonstrated executable enforcement.

The proposed implication returns true outside the urgency condition; this must mean inapplicability rather than substantive compliance. Its Boolean compliance label also does not independently preserve the source's should/please modality.
The prose retains uncertainty about completed filing and later follow-up, but no executable child preserves the separation between pre-launch contact and the post-implementation submission trigger.
Both actual children are UNENCODED with E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE; executable preservation of the parent's conditional assumptions and unresolved exception attachment cannot be verified.

The prose retains indivisibility and principal-economic-character treatment as conditional premises, but no supplied authority establishes either a dominance test or the legal consequences of separability.

The parent's explicit assessment that the competing reading is materially less supported is not expressly retained, although its lack of authority and inability to determine the exception remain explicit.

additional_concerns: Executable meaning is unavailable: the supplied representation reports an unsupported '+' operator or arity. This establishes an assessment limitation, not a substantive omission or conflict.

The indirect-exposure examples are non-exhaustive under footnote 2. Neither those examples nor the CLO definition establishes that every holding in a named instrument contributes its full value to private-market exposure.

No supplied methodology resolves look-through measurement, double counting, valuation timing or temporary threshold crossings. Simple addition cannot be validated without knowing what its operands measure.

The source does not resolve persistence or declassification following a later exposure decline. The question appropriately limits its temporal scope.

No executable restrictions or permissions can be inspected from the error representation. In particular, the separate 15% investment limit, suitability duties and document-update timing must not become extra conditions for classification.

additional_concerns: The discretionary-factor omissions identify limits of executable coverage, not necessarily code defects. A formula consuming an evidenced SFC designation need not reproduce the regulator's deliberation. It must not be presented as independently deciding whether designation is warranted.

Footnote 7 qualifies the holistic designation assessment as concerning exposure below 50% of NAV. The representation does not encode that qualification within designation assessment. Its disjunction is nevertheless compatible with the two classification routes: exposure at or above 50% already suffices. The source does not establish that a previously operative designation ceases upon a threshold crossing, so adding a current below-50% guard could introduce an unsupported restriction.

The factor list also includes home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions in d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. Neither that factor nor the holistic, non-exhaustive assessment is executable here. If the candidate were expanded to generate designation decisions, implementing only the factors covered by the required pairs would be incomplete.

The aggregate input refers to 'the applicable methodology', but the supplied source does not specify a calculation procedure for indirect exposure, look-through, valuation timing or avoidance of double counting. Missing measurement evidence is correctly kept unresolved in the input description; no particular methodology has been validated. Any additional authority needed to establish that methodology is unidentified and must not be assigned an invented dependency ID.

The mandatory trigger concerns total direct and indirect exposure. Footnote 1's 15% direct-investment limit does not replace the 50% aggregate threshold or establish that the latter is unreachable. UT Code 7.3 is not supplied; it would be needed to reconstruct the separate investment-limit regime, not to establish the narrow classification trigger.

The LAF exclusion is stated directly in footnote 6 and appears in scope. The separate LAF circular is not supplied, and is_laf remains a judgment input. Assessing an ambiguous fund's LAF status or its separate regulatory treatment may require that authority; the packet provides no identifiable dependency mapping for it. Exclusion here does not establish non-complex status under another regime.

The runtime rule that any conflicting fact blocks evaluation even on an unselected branch is an added evidentiary policy, not a requirement stated by the circular. It can withhold a result when one classification route is otherwise established. Distinguish an evaluator's refusal to resolve conflicting records from the legal sufficiency of an established trigger.

The question's false_means phrase 'neither ... is established' could be read as mere absence of evidence. The representation instead requires known false inputs for an in-scope FALSE result and preserves missing evidence as UNKNOWN. Keep that distinction explicit; missing designation records do not establish absence of designation.

The consultation claim's OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata is stronger than the source's 'encouraged' wording if treated as mandatory. Its prose statement preserves the source qualification. Consultation must not be added as a prerequisite to classification or as permission to treat uncertainty as non-complex status.

No supplied external dependency has a non-null source_hash, and the three unbound IDs are not mapped to named authorities. None can be marked AVAILABLE. The missing sales authorities remain unresolved even though their downstream requirements are outside this typed question.

The packet supports the retained circular's propositions, not an independently verified statement of current law. No actual assessment date, portfolio evidence or designation record is supplied, so these checks establish neither a particular Fund's classification nor compliance with downstream duties.

additional_concerns: OMITS identifies unimplemented upstream assessments, not necessarily defects relative to the exact typed question. A formula consuming an evidenced designation need not reproduce the SFC's deliberation. It must not be presented as independently determining whether designation is warranted. No prior dispute is resolved merely by repeating a label.

Footnote 7 places the holistic designation assessment below 50% of NAV. The disjunction does not encode that qualification, but exposure at or above 50% already suffices. The source does not establish that an existing designation ceases when exposure crosses the threshold; adding a current below-50% guard to operative_sfc_designation could impose an unsupported restriction.

The non-exhaustive designation factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions in d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. Any extension that generates designation decisions would need to account for that factor and the holistic assessment, without converting individual factors into automatic triggers. Applicable home-regulator measures would require separate evidence if used; none is identified here.

The aggregate input's 'applicable methodology' is not a supplied calculation procedure. Look-through, derivative exposure measurement, valuation timing and avoidance of double counting remain unimplemented and unvalidated. Which additional authority, if any, is necessary to settle those choices is uncertain; no dependency ID can be assigned. Before operational use, identify the methodology and its evidentiary or authoritative basis.

The 15% direct-investment limit in footnote 1 does not replace the 50% total direct-and-indirect classification threshold. UT Code 7.3 is missing and would be needed to reconstruct the separate investment-limit regime. Its absence does not prevent source support for the narrow classification trigger.

The LAF exclusion is directly supported and represented in scope. The separate LAF circular identified by footnote 6 is missing. It may be required to resolve disputed LAF status or separate regulatory treatment; no supplied dependency mapping identifies it. OUT_OF_SCOPE must not imply non-complex status under another regime.

The runtime provision 'A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch.' adds an evidence-handling restriction not stated by the circular. It can withhold a result despite an otherwise established sufficient route, or despite a scope fact that would otherwise settle exclusion. This is an operational refusal to evaluate, not an additional legal classification condition.

The question's false_means wording 'neither aggregate exposure of at least 50% of NAV nor an operative SFC designation is established' risks confusing lack of evidence with established absence. Within known scope, the representation requires both route inputs to be FALSE for FALSE; missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless another established route determines TRUE.

Consultation is encouraged, and product risk rating is qualified by 'if applicable'. Neither may be converted into a mandatory classification prerequisite. Conversely, consultation or unresolved measurement does not grant permission to treat a Fund as non-complex.

All three supplied external dependency records have null source_hash values and no identifying mappings. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and none can reliably be assigned to a named missing authority. Source unit IDs are not dependency IDs.

The Internal Product Approval Process circular identified in d4148dd852cee.u36.5149 and footnote 9, and the Advertising Guidelines identified in d4148dd852cee.u42.6275 and footnote 10, are also absent. They would be necessary to reconstruct those broader incorporated regimes, but are not needed for the narrow distributor statements or classification output assessed here.

The supported BDC claims concern the circular's description. Independent verification under the US Investment Company Act of 1940 would require additional authority and is not established by this packet. Likewise, the possibility of later SFC updates does not prove that updates exist or apply.

The exposure-definition and open-ended-example claims are relevant to upstream input construction but are not executed by either representation. Their OMITS assessments identify that boundary; they do not establish a Boolean-rule defect or an exhaustive asset filter.

Both representations say: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." This is an operational evidence policy, not a restriction supplied by the circular. It can prevent a classification answer despite an independently established sufficient route. It should be distinguished from a legal conclusion that the threshold or designation has ceased to apply.

Both representations say: "No UNKNOWN, CONFLICT or ERROR is converted to a known Boolean." This avoids inferring absence from missing evidence, but the circular does not itself prescribe these computational states. A negative answer requires established negative route facts within established scope.

The first candidate’s false_means wording, "neither aggregate exposure of at least 50% of NAV nor an operative SFC designation is established", could be read as mere absence of evidence. Its executable semantics instead require both route facts to be FALSE. The wording should preserve that distinction.

No unsupported automatic permission to sell, exemption from suitability, or conclusion of general non-complex status appears in the executable rules. Neither consultation, home-regulator restrictions nor compliance with the 15% limit should be added as a classification prerequisite or automatic trigger.

The consultation claim’s statement correctly says encouraged, while its kind is OBLIGATION. That metadata is potentially stronger than the source and should not support a mandatory-duty inference; it is not a demonstrated defect in either classification executable.

Footnote 7 situates the holistic warranted-designation assessment below 50% of NAV. The OR formulas preserve outcomes for established threshold values because classification already follows automatically at or above 50%. They do not establish designation persistence, withdrawal or treatment of subsequent exposure changes.

The designation-authority dispute reflects two assessment levels: the circular establishes the generic discretionary power, while applying a particular designation requires its decision and operative terms. NONE_DECLARED below addresses the generic claim; the missing decision evidence remains an explicit follow-up rather than an assumed negative fact.

additional_concerns: These assessments concern the supplied source and declared representation. No Fund-specific evidence, executable implementation or runtime results are supplied; the labels do not establish a classification for any actual Fund.

Footnote 7 expressly places the holistic discretionary assessment below 50% of NAV. The representation does not expressly guard the designation branch with a below-threshold condition. For consistent known Boolean inputs, threshold OR designation and threshold OR (NOT threshold AND designation) give the same classification result. Thus the missing guard is a source-context omission, not an established output defect; it must not imply that the automatic route requires a separate SFC decision.

The global conflict rule blocks evaluation even when an independently established route would suffice. For example, a conflict about designation can block a known at-least-50% threshold result. This is an additional evidentiary restriction imposed by the runtime, not a condition stated by the circular. Whether it is an intended operational safeguard remains unresolved.

The circular does not supply exposure measurement, look-through, valuation, netting or aggregation methods in the retained text. The representation acknowledges that these are unresolved input judgments. If applying the rule requires further measurement authority, that authority is missing and must be identified; no supplied dependency ID can presently be matched to it.

An assessment relying on the discretionary route needs the actual Fund-specific SFC designation and evidence of its temporal applicability. Those materials are not supplied. A false designation input likewise requires adequate evidence; an unsearched history cannot establish absence. No identifiable dependency ID for such materials is provided.

The supplied text does not establish effective dates, designation persistence or later amendments. Applying this rule at a particular time requires those matters to be resolved where material. The mere possibility of later updates does not establish that an update exists.

The three supplied external dependency IDs all have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying their authorities. None can be marked AVAILABLE or reliably assigned to a particular missing authority. All pair-level NONE_DECLARED assessments concern support for the narrow claims, not completeness of evidence for a Fund-specific determination.

Additional external authorities expressly referenced by the retained source but not supplied with identifiable mappings are UT Code section 7.3; the LAF circular refNo=25EC9; Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5; Chapter 6 of the Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms and relevant FAQs; the internal product-approval circular refNo=16EC11; and the cited advertising guidelines. Their absence does not defeat claims stated directly in this circular, but it prevents assessment of their full incorporated requirements.

Footnote 1 states a 15% limit on direct private-asset investments or exposures under UT Code section 7.3. That separate investment restriction must not be substituted for the 50% aggregate classification threshold, used to cap observed exposure artificially, or treated as permission for all exposures below 50%. Overall investment-limit compliance is outside this question.

Footnote 6 excludes a category of assessed Funds. It does not exclude every listed closed-ended holding from indirect exposure. In particular, the BDC description must not be conflated with the LAF exclusion.

The factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements or conditions under unit d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. These are not represented as executable factor assessments. Like the listed asset and Fund characteristics, they inform SFC discretion and do not themselves substitute for an actual designation.

The consultation statement is supported as encouragement. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata would overstate the source if a downstream process treated it as a mandatory consultation condition or an independent classification trigger.

A false classification result does not establish overall compliance, permission to distribute without other requirements, or absence of classification under another regime. OUT_OF_SCOPE for a LAF likewise does not establish that the Fund is non-complex under its separate regime.

The discretionary-factor and definition omissions are upstream assessment boundaries, not automatic instructions to add predicates to the Boolean rule. Their proper treatment depends on whether a separate, adequately supported input-assessment process exists.

Footnote 7 places the holistic discretionary assessment in cases below 50% of NAV. The representation does not explicitly guard its designation branch with that condition. For known consistent Boolean inputs, threshold OR designation equals threshold OR (NOT threshold AND designation). Under the declared uncertainty semantics, they can differ: an unknown threshold and a true designation yield TRUE in the supplied representation, but UNKNOWN with an added below-threshold guard. The packet does not establish that re-testing the current threshold is necessary to rely on an actual applicable designation; adding the guard is therefore not an established repair.

The automatic route requires total direct and indirect exposure of 50% or more, including exactly 50%. It does not require a separate SFC designation. Discretionary factors, whether individually or collectively present, must not be converted into an automatic designation rule.

The runtime states: 'A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch.' A designation conflict can therefore block a known threshold result, and an irrelevant conflict may block scope handling. This is an additional evidentiary restriction not stated in the circular. Whether it is an intended operational safeguard remains unresolved.

Exposure measurement, look-through, valuation, netting and aggregation are not implemented or resolved by the supplied source. Any additional authority needed to resolve them is missing and unidentified. A broad input description is not evidence that upstream exposure calculations faithfully implement the circular.

Reliance on designation requires the actual Fund-specific SFC decision and evidence of temporal applicability. Neither is supplied. An unsearched designation history cannot establish a false input. Missing holdings, measurement or designation evidence must remain unknown rather than be treated as evidence of absence.

The supplied source does not establish the circular's effective date, designation persistence or applicable subsequent amendments. Its statement that examples may be updated does not establish that an update exists. Assessment-time applicability remains unresolved where material.

All three supplied external dependencies have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying their authorities. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and no particular missing authority can reliably be mapped to those IDs. Pair-level NONE_DECLARED assessments concern the narrow source-supported claims, not completeness of the evidence needed for a Fund-specific application.

External authorities referenced but not supplied with identifiable dependency mappings include UT Code section 7.3; the LAF circular refNo=25EC9; Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5; Chapter 6 of the Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms and relevant FAQs; the internal product-approval circular refNo=16EC11; and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes. Their full requirements remain unchecked. The circular's source-attributed BDC description does not independently verify the US Investment Company Act of 1940.

Footnote 1 states a separate 15% investment limit for direct private-asset investments or exposures. That limit must not replace the 50% aggregate classification threshold, artificially cap observed exposures, or imply permission for exposures below 50%. Investment-limit compliance is outside the typed question.

The LAF exclusion concerns the assessed Fund, not every listed closed-ended holding in its portfolio. The BDC description must not be conflated with the exclusion or used to remove BDC-related indirect exposure from aggregation.

The non-exhaustive designation factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements or conditions in unit d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. They are not executed by the formula. If a separate factor assessment is undertaken, any applicable home-regulator instruments would need to be supplied; their existence, content and dependency mapping are unresolved.

The consultation statement is encouragement. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata would overstate the source if used to impose mandatory consultation, suspend the automatic threshold pending consultation, or create another classification trigger.

A FALSE result addresses only the two circular-based classification routes within established scope. It establishes neither overall compliance nor permission to distribute without other requirements. OUT_OF_SCOPE for a LAF likewise does not determine its treatment under the separate LAF regime.

OMITS for definitions, exposure interpretation and discretionary factors identifies the boundary of the executable representation. It does not by itself require adding predicates to the formula. With otherwise established scope and an applicable SFC designation, unknown NAV produces UNKNOWN and nonpositive NAV produces OUT_OF_SCOPE. The source supplies no such restriction on the designation route. A measurement-validity check and a legal-scope exclusion have different consequences.

The arithmetic in node.ad3ed6f7c586444ec7213491 expresses twice the aggregate exposure being at least NAV. It preserves the inclusive half-NAV boundary for suitable exact, commensurate inputs; this does not verify the upstream valuation method, look-through treatment, overlap handling or numeric implementation.

Footnote 7 expressly situates holistic designation assessment below 50%. Both candidates may consume an actual applicable designation without independently recreating that assessment, but neither establishes the validity of the designation process or authorizes a manager to substitute its own factor assessment for an SFC decision.

The packet contains no exposure methodology, Fund-specific designation decision, assessment date, or rules governing persistence after threshold changes. These gaps do not invalidate the circular's stated routes, but they limit any Fund-specific determination.

The labels OMITS for exposure definitions and designation factors identify unimplemented upstream assessments. They do not establish that the classification formulas require instrument-level or regulator-decision logic, and they do not authorize pruning those source claims.

The three supplied external dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no authority-name mappings. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and assigning any of them to UT Code paragraph 7.3 or footnote 8 authorities would invent a catalogue match.

If a Fund's LAF category is disputed, the LAF circular identified in footnote 6 may be needed. It is not supplied or mapped to a dependency ID. Its absence does not undermine the express exclusion, and exclusion from this circular does not establish exemption under other rules.

Claim claim.e97a5ab05dba08850901077d faithfully says consultation is encouraged. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata could nevertheless be read more strongly than the source; neither mandatory consultation nor automatic classification pending consultation is supported.

The global CONFLICT blocking rule is a declared evidence-handling policy, not a classification condition established by the circular. It can prevent a Boolean result despite another independently sufficient route; that operational consequence should remain distinct from a substantive finding that classification is not required.

Neither a FALSE classification result nor OUT_OF_SCOPE establishes compliance with the separate 15% investment limit, sale requirements, disclosure duties or other applicable rules. The candidate questions appropriately limit their negative-result meanings.

The packet does not establish that a later update exists or that the supplied aggregate would ignore it. An omitted update mechanism must not be treated as proof of stale or wrong exposure data.

The global rule that a conflicting fact anywhere in the dependency closure blocks evaluation can prevent a result otherwise established by an independent route. The formula gives a classification result only. It does not establish compliance with the direct-investment limit, disclosures, distributor duties or complex-product sales requirements. PRESERVES findings concern the stated classification relationship using supplied judgment facts. The representation does not establish LAF status, measure aggregate exposure, perform holistic assessment or prove an operative designation. The OMITS findings for channel identification and home-regulator factors identify this delegated work, not established Boolean defects.

The authority dispute for the general designation power admits two scopes: the circular suffices to establish the claim, while applying the route requires missing fund-specific decision evidence. NONE_DECLARED is proposed for the former; MISSING remains appropriate if the assessed dependency is the particular operative decision. No decision is inferred from the absence of supplied evidence.

The authority dispute for home-regulator conditions similarly separates a supported general factor list from an unresolved application inquiry. No extra authority is needed for the list; which home-regulator instruments, if any, are necessary for a particular assessment remains uncertain.

The runtime states: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." This can block classification despite an independently established threshold route, or block OUT_OF_SCOPE despite established LAF status. It is an additional evidence-handling policy, not a restriction imposed by the circular; it must not be presented as a substantive classification exception.

The unrestricted designation disjunct does not alter an ordinary Boolean classification outcome at or above 50%, because the threshold independently suffices. It nevertheless does not encode footnote 7's restriction on the described holistic assessment and cannot establish the discretionary power's scope above the threshold.

Named intermediaries, a home-regulator restriction, enhanced scrutiny, missing disclosure, or breach of the 15% investment limit do not independently establish an SFC designation. The representation supplies no such extra route. Nor does it create an existing-fund exemption or an update-related classification grace period.

The packet does not establish measurement dates, valuation, look-through, netting, aggregation, designation duration or classification persistence after exposure falls below 50%. The temporal input convention does not resolve those issues. FALSE means only that both retained routes are established absent on the stated assessment basis; OUT_OF_SCOPE does not mean non-complex under another regime.

The three supplied external dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying the authorities they represent. None supports AVAILABLE, and none can safely be assigned to a missing authority. Empty dependency_ids preserve this unresolved mapping.

The suitability claim is supported as the circular's summary, with incorporated scope reserved. Reading its actor label as an unconditional duty on every possible seller would exceed what is established here; missing incorporated qualifications are not evidence of a defect in this classification formula.
