units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has observed that investment funds may, for asset allocation and yield enhancement purposes, gain exposure to private credit and private equity (collectively, private market assets) via: direct exposure through investments in bank or non-bank direct lending in the form of loans or equities to unlisted companies (direct exposure)1; or indirect exposures2 including through investments in business development companies (BDCs)3, collateralised loan obligations (CLOs)4 or financial derivative instruments5.

This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard. Funds with direct or indirect exposure to private market assets are required to observe the enhanced disclosure requirements set out in this circular. A Fund may be subject to enhanced scrutiny by the SFC in some cases and be classified as a complex product for distribution, where appropriate.

Direct investment in private market assets generally carries higher inherent risks than publicly listed securities, as these assets are typically illiquid, hard to value, and subject to limited regulatory oversight; they also have higher credit risks and thus higher risk of default. While indirect exposures to the private market assets may not present the same level of risk as direct investments, recent market developments have raised concerns about these indirect exposures, such as the rising default risks of underlying investments for private credit funds, widening price-to-NAV discount for listed BDCs, etc. In addition, certain indirect exposures may lack transparency about the underlying private market assets, as they involve layered structures or complex financial instruments such that retail investors may not reasonably understand the features and risks of these indirect exposures.

Considering that retail investors in Hong Kong may have limited familiarity with private market assets and their associated risks, fund managers should ensure that investors are provided with a clear, sufficiently complete and balanced picture of the characteristics, nature and extent of risks associated with various types of exposures a Fund may have to private market assets. Fund managers should also, among other things, ensure that the distributors chosen are appropriate for covering the target market of their Funds.
Enhanced disclosure in offering documents
If a Fund may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, its fund manager should ensure that the Fund’s offering document (including the key facts statement (KFS)) clearly discloses:

(i)        the extent and the means of access of exposure (eg, up to [x]% of the Fund’s NAV is invested in listed BDCs which primarily invest in private market assets; [x – y%] of the Fund’s NAV will gain exposure to private loans via investment in senior tranche of CLOs);

(ii)       the nature and characteristics of the underlying private market assets (eg, the minimum credit rating of the CLOs in which the Fund invests, TRSs on an index comprising unsecuritised broadly syndicated loans); and

(iii)      in the offering documents (and where appropriate, the KFS), the key risks associated with the Fund’s exposure to the specific types of private market assets it directly or indirectly invests in, including the impact and implications to the Fund and its investors (e.g. the limited liquidity and lack of transparency of the underlying private market assets of the BDCs can make them more challenging to value, and these valuation uncertainties may negatively impact the BDC’s NAV and hence the Fund’s NAV).
Complex product designation

A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
•        the aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets of the Fund;
•        the Fund's overall investment strategy, portfolio composition, and liquidity and/or risk profile;

•        the extent, nature and characteristics of the specific asset types in which the Fund invests (eg, the tranches and credit ratings of CLOs; the structure, tranches and underlying assets of SRTs); and
•        any distribution restrictions, requirements or other conditions as may be imposed by the Fund’s home regulators.
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.
Target market identification and distributor selection

The SFC wishes to remind fund managers to observe the requirements set out in the “Circular to Product Providers of SFC-authorized unit trusts and mutual funds, SFC-authorized investment-linked assurance schemes and SFC-authorized unlisted structured investment products – Guidance on Internal Product Approval Process”9, which outlines, among others, the requirements regarding target market identification and distributor selection for SFC-authorised funds.

Fund managers should carefully identify the target market to ensure that the Fund, including its underlying investments and associated risks, would be generally understood by the target market and that the Fund’s investment objectives and risk/return profile match the needs and risk appetite of the target market. They should also ensure that the distributors chosen are appropriate for covering the target market identified, have the necessary product knowledge to understand the Fund (including whether the Fund is a complex product) and to assign an appropriate product risk rating (if applicable) for the Fund, and advise investors accordingly.

Fund managers are further reminded that the marketing materials of SFC-authorised funds must comply with the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes10, which provide, among other requirements, that advertisements of a Fund should be fair and present a balanced picture of the Fund with adequate risk disclosures.
Others

When seeking the SFC’s authorisation for any new funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, the fund may be subject to the SFC’s closer scrutiny. In some cases, the SFC may not process the fund under the Fund Authorisation Simple Track (FASTrack).

For existing SFC-authorised funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, fund managers are expected to undertake a review of their funds, take appropriate actions including updating the Fund’s offering documents as soon as practicable, and ensure necessary and proper communications with the distributors in light of the guidance provided under this circular (in particular, with respect to paragraphs 9 and 10 above). Fund managers are encouraged to consult the SFC at the earliest opportunity if they are in doubt regarding complex product classification of their Funds.
If you wish to seek clarification of any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission
1 Direct investments in/exposures to private assets fall within the investment limit of 15% of a Fund’s total net asset value (NAV) under 7.3 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds (UT Code).
2 The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.
3 BDCs are close-ended funds registered under the US Investment Company Act of 1940, which primarily invest in debt and equity of small and mid-sized companies in the US.
4 CLOs are securities backed by a pool of debt, typically leveraged loans and broadly syndicated loans, or direct lending to unlisted companies.
5 For example, Total Return Swaps on indices with exposure to leveraged loans or broadly syndicated loans (TRSs), or Significant Risk Transfers with underlying assets that are corporate loans (SRTs).

6 Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs). For LAFs, please refer to the circular on LAFs: https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/products/product-authorization/doc?refNo=25EC9
7 In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.

8 Paragraph 5.5 of the SFC’s Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission and Chapter 6 of the SFC’s Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms, and the relevant Frequently Asked Questions.

9 Issued by the SFC on 30 April 2014 and subsequently updated on 4 March 2016. Please refer to: https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/products/product-authorization/doc?refNo=16EC11

10 Latest version issued by the SFC in April 2013. Please refer to: https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/advertising-guidelines-applicable-to-collective-investment-schemes/Advertising-Guidelines--Applicable-to-Collective-Investment-Schemes-Authorized-under-the-Product-Cod.pdf

citations.quote: This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard.

A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.
Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.
The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.

frame_assumptions: Both assessments must concern the identical fund F, as a whole distributed product, at the identical assessment instant t. Neither individual holdings, intermediary funds, investors nor transactions are separate threshold units.

The SFC in both frames is the same authorising and designating institution. Managers, distributors and investors retain their distinct roles; their actions are not substitutes for an SFC designation. Home regulators appear expressly only in the left frame, as contextual inputs to SFC discretion, not as alternative designation authorities.

Both frames must use the same private-market asset category: private credit and private equity. The right frame's explicit TRS and SRT examples fall within the left frame's financial-derivative category only insofar as they provide relevant private-market exposure. Neither list limits the indirect-exposure universe.

Both frames must distinguish underlying private-market assets from intermediary holdings and instruments. Their direct and indirect components must be determined by the same established methodology, including look-through, derivatives, netting, layered holdings and prevention of inappropriate double counting.

Both frames must express each exposure component and fund NAV in the same exact valuation unit U at t. No currency, scale, valuation convention or rounding equivalence is inferred from the labels 'valuation units' and 'accounting units'. The identity mapping is conditional on exact normalization to U.
Authorisation, LAF category and designation applicability must concern F at t. The left category fact is interpreted contemporaneously with the other facts, consistently with its assessment frame.
Positive NAV is a shared model-domain premise, not an additional legal rule established by the quoted circular. Outside the shared scope, neither model supplies a classification answer.

No effective date, measurement frequency, averaging window, temporary-crossing treatment, cure period or automatic declassification rule is established here. Document-update timing is distinct from classification timing.

Offering documents, manager communications and home-regulator conditions remain contextual distinctions. Their omission from one frame's object list does not eliminate their possible legal relevance, but neither formal predicate directly tests them.
This proposal establishes neither these premises nor legal equivalence. Referenced but unavailable instruments may impose additional classification and distribution requirements.

Within shared scope, both result expressions reduce by associativity of exact integer addition to (or (>= (+ (+ common_direct common_indirect) (+ common_direct common_indirect)) common_nav) common_designation). This preserves the inclusive 50% boundary without division or rounding.

evidence.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has observed that investment funds may, for asset allocation and yield enhancement purposes, gain exposure to private credit and private equity (collectively, private market assets) via: direct exposure through investments in bank or non-bank direct lending in the form of loans or equities to unlisted companies (direct exposure)1; or indirect exposures2 including through investments in business development companies (BDCs)3, collateralised loan obligations (CLOs)4 or financial derivative instruments5.

A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
7 In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.
2 The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.
5 For example, Total Return Swaps on indices with exposure to leveraged loans or broadly syndicated loans (TRSs), or Significant Risk Transfers with underlying assets that are corporate loans (SRTs).
1 Direct investments in/exposures to private assets fall within the investment limit of 15% of a Fund’s total net asset value (NAV) under 7.3 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds (UT Code).

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has observed that investment funds may, for asset allocation and yield enhancement purposes, gain exposure to private credit and private equity (collectively, private market assets) via: direct exposure through investments in bank or non-bank direct lending in the form of loans or equities to unlisted companies (direct exposure)1; or indirect exposures2 including through investments in business development companies (BDCs)3, collateralised loan obligations (CLOs)4 or financial derivative instruments5.

This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard. Funds with direct or indirect exposure to private market assets are required to observe the enhanced disclosure requirements set out in this circular. A Fund may be subject to enhanced scrutiny by the SFC in some cases and be classified as a complex product for distribution, where appropriate.

Direct investment in private market assets generally carries higher inherent risks than publicly listed securities, as these assets are typically illiquid, hard to value, and subject to limited regulatory oversight; they also have higher credit risks and thus higher risk of default. While indirect exposures to the private market assets may not present the same level of risk as direct investments, recent market developments have raised concerns about these indirect exposures, such as the rising default risks of underlying investments for private credit funds, widening price-to-NAV discount for listed BDCs, etc. In addition, certain indirect exposures may lack transparency about the underlying private market assets, as they involve layered structures or complex financial instruments such that retail investors may not reasonably understand the features and risks of these indirect exposures.

Considering that retail investors in Hong Kong may have limited familiarity with private market assets and their associated risks, fund managers should ensure that investors are provided with a clear, sufficiently complete and balanced picture of the characteristics, nature and extent of risks associated with various types of exposures a Fund may have to private market assets. Fund managers should also, among other things, ensure that the distributors chosen are appropriate for covering the target market of their Funds.
Enhanced disclosure in offering documents
If a Fund may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, its fund manager should ensure that the Fund’s offering document (including the key facts statement (KFS)) clearly discloses:

(i)        the extent and the means of access of exposure (eg, up to [x]% of the Fund’s NAV is invested in listed BDCs which primarily invest in private market assets; [x – y%] of the Fund’s NAV will gain exposure to private loans via investment in senior tranche of CLOs);

(ii)       the nature and characteristics of the underlying private market assets (eg, the minimum credit rating of the CLOs in which the Fund invests, TRSs on an index comprising unsecuritised broadly syndicated loans); and

(iii)      in the offering documents (and where appropriate, the KFS), the key risks associated with the Fund’s exposure to the specific types of private market assets it directly or indirectly invests in, including the impact and implications to the Fund and its investors (e.g. the limited liquidity and lack of transparency of the underlying private market assets of the BDCs can make them more challenging to value, and these valuation uncertainties may negatively impact the BDC’s NAV and hence the Fund’s NAV).
Complex product designation

A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
•        the aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets of the Fund;
•        the Fund's overall investment strategy, portfolio composition, and liquidity and/or risk profile;

•        the extent, nature and characteristics of the specific asset types in which the Fund invests (eg, the tranches and credit ratings of CLOs; the structure, tranches and underlying assets of SRTs); and
•        any distribution restrictions, requirements or other conditions as may be imposed by the Fund’s home regulators.
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.
Target market identification and distributor selection

The SFC wishes to remind fund managers to observe the requirements set out in the “Circular to Product Providers of SFC-authorized unit trusts and mutual funds, SFC-authorized investment-linked assurance schemes and SFC-authorized unlisted structured investment products – Guidance on Internal Product Approval Process”9, which outlines, among others, the requirements regarding target market identification and distributor selection for SFC-authorised funds.

Fund managers should carefully identify the target market to ensure that the Fund, including its underlying investments and associated risks, would be generally understood by the target market and that the Fund’s investment objectives and risk/return profile match the needs and risk appetite of the target market. They should also ensure that the distributors chosen are appropriate for covering the target market identified, have the necessary product knowledge to understand the Fund (including whether the Fund is a complex product) and to assign an appropriate product risk rating (if applicable) for the Fund, and advise investors accordingly.

Fund managers are further reminded that the marketing materials of SFC-authorised funds must comply with the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes10, which provide, among other requirements, that advertisements of a Fund should be fair and present a balanced picture of the Fund with adequate risk disclosures.
Others

When seeking the SFC’s authorisation for any new funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, the fund may be subject to the SFC’s closer scrutiny. In some cases, the SFC may not process the fund under the Fund Authorisation Simple Track (FASTrack).

For existing SFC-authorised funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, fund managers are expected to undertake a review of their funds, take appropriate actions including updating the Fund’s offering documents as soon as practicable, and ensure necessary and proper communications with the distributors in light of the guidance provided under this circular (in particular, with respect to paragraphs 9 and 10 above). Fund managers are encouraged to consult the SFC at the earliest opportunity if they are in doubt regarding complex product classification of their Funds.
If you wish to seek clarification of any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission
1 Direct investments in/exposures to private assets fall within the investment limit of 15% of a Fund’s total net asset value (NAV) under 7.3 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds (UT Code).
2 The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.
3 BDCs are close-ended funds registered under the US Investment Company Act of 1940, which primarily invest in debt and equity of small and mid-sized companies in the US.
4 CLOs are securities backed by a pool of debt, typically leveraged loans and broadly syndicated loans, or direct lending to unlisted companies.
5 For example, Total Return Swaps on indices with exposure to leveraged loans or broadly syndicated loans (TRSs), or Significant Risk Transfers with underlying assets that are corporate loans (SRTs).

6 Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs). For LAFs, please refer to the circular on LAFs: https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/products/product-authorization/doc?refNo=25EC9
7 In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.

8 Paragraph 5.5 of the SFC’s Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission and Chapter 6 of the SFC’s Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms, and the relevant Frequently Asked Questions.

9 Issued by the SFC on 30 April 2014 and subsequently updated on 4 March 2016. Please refer to: https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/products/product-authorization/doc?refNo=16EC11

10 Latest version issued by the SFC in April 2013. Please refer to: https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/advertising-guidelines-applicable-to-collective-investment-schemes/Advertising-Guidelines--Applicable-to-Collective-Investment-Schemes-Authorized-under-the-Product-Cod.pdf

frame_assumptions: Both assessments must concern the identical fund F as a whole distributed product at the identical assessment instant t. Individual holdings, intermediary funds, investors and distribution transactions are not separate threshold units.

Both frames refer to the same SFC as authorising and designating institution. Managers, distributors and investors retain their separate roles. Home regulators, expressly listed only in the left frame, provide potential inputs to SFC discretion; their restrictions are not themselves SFC designations.

Both frames must use the same private-market asset category, comprising private credit and private equity. BDCs, CLOs, TRSs and SRTs are intermediary holdings or instruments where relevant, distinct from their underlying assets. The examples do not exhaust qualifying indirect exposure.

The direct and indirect components must use the same separately established measurement and aggregation methodology, including treatment of derivatives, look-through, layered holdings, netting and overlapping exposures. Similar variable descriptions do not establish this premise.

For the proposed identity expressions, the original integer inputs on both sides must already use the identical exact unit U, valuation basis and scale at t. Calling one unit an accounting unit and the other a valuation unit does not establish equality. Differently scaled inputs require a separately specified exact conversion before this proposal applies; no rounding at the 50% boundary is permitted.
Authorisation, LAF category and designation applicability must concern F at t. In particular, the left LAF category determination must be contemporaneous with the other assessment facts.

The shared model scope requires SFC authorisation for public offering in Hong Kong, exclusion of LAFs, and positive NAV. Positive NAV is a formal model-domain premise, not a separately established legal requirement from the quoted text.

An applicable designation and an operative designation must denote the same actual SFC decision concerning F and operating at t. Potential grounds, enhanced scrutiny, manager opinions and home-regulator conditions do not establish that decision.

No commencement date, averaging window, reassessment cadence, temporary-crossing treatment, cure period or automatic declassification rule is supplied by this proposal. The timing of document updates remains distinct from classification timing.

Offering documents and distributor communications, expressly listed as objects only in the right frame, and the discretionary factors expressly listed only in the left frame retain their contextual roles. Neither formal classification predicate directly measures their adequacy or compliance.

The proposal does not establish any factual or frame premise, complete the unavailable referenced instruments, or establish legal equivalence. Its potential correspondence is limited to the supplied classification predicates.

Both original results use TRUE_IS_SATISFIED. Neither permitted output enum represents that classification meaning. The required TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT entries are serialization placeholders only, not compliance findings; the proposal cannot establish a faithful output-label bridge under this enum restriction.

left_frame.temporal_basis: One assessment time with contemporaneous exposure and NAV measurements and an SFC designation applicable at that time. The source supplies no precise measurement frequency, commencement date or threshold-crossing cure period.
left_frame.unit_of_assessment: One Fund as a whole at an identified distribution assessment time, aggregating its relevant direct and indirect private-market exposures.

assumptions: All common facts refer to the fixed fund F and assessment instant t identified in the frame premises; all common integer amounts use the identical exact unit U and shared established methodology.

Each original fact has the identity expression specified below only conditional on the frame premises. The proposal itself supplies no evidence that particular fund measurements or institutional facts coincide.
Both scope expressions become (and common_authorised (not common_laf) (> common_nav (integer 0))). A false scope yields no classification answer; an excluded LAF is not thereby non-complex.

Within established scope, substitution makes the left result (or (>= (+ (+ common_direct common_indirect) (+ common_direct common_indirect)) common_nav) common_designation) and the right result (or (>= (+ common_direct common_indirect common_direct common_indirect) common_nav) common_designation). Associativity of exact integer addition makes these predicates equal, conditional on the stated interpretations of addition and comparison.

The repeated sum implements the inclusive 50% threshold without division or rounding. This correspondence assumes exact arithmetic without overflow. The separate 15% direct-investment limit is not substituted for this classification threshold.

An actual operative SFC designation is an independent classification route. Below-threshold exposure alone does not establish that no designation exists, and factors supporting discretionary designation do not automatically create one.

Missing facts remain unknown, not false or zero. Once scope is established, a known true branch can establish the classification result despite uncertainty in the other branch. A false result requires both classification branches to be established false.

A false result concerns only the modeled bases at t; it establishes neither non-complex status under other instruments nor immunity from later designation. A true result identifies complex-product classification, not a prohibition or overall distribution compliance.

TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT is included on each side solely because the required schema admits no TRUE_IS_SATISFIED value. Neither supplied predicate means compliant. These enum entries must not be relied on as semantic output mappings; a faithful executable output bridge requires a classification-satisfaction convention.
The exact source quotations support the categories and classification structure, but do not establish the valuation method, actual fund facts, temporal premises or legal equivalence.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

evidence.quote: 1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC.

frame_assumptions: Both frames assess the same identified change to the same fund, including every objective, policy or restriction component and every product feature involved in that change.
The SFC, proposing management company and home regulator named in each frame are the same respective actors; identity is a premise, not established by this proposal.
Both frames use the same assessment date and the same application covering the change. Pending status is fixed by SFC receipt and absence of approval or authorisation at 28 November 2025.
The two European-UCITS classifications and the two UK-UCITS classifications coincide only if the fund's domicile and authorisation facts satisfy the quoted circular definition.
Satisfaction of home requirements and whether requirements are met refer to the same complete set of applicable home-jurisdiction requirements for this change.
The specific effective date governs the circular's general immediate-effect wording. The transition is interpreted to preserve the existing process for a qualifying pending application.
Neither frame treats post-vetting as prior approval, or failure of removal eligibility as proof of an independent approval obligation.

actors: SFC, which receives applications and administers prior approval and post-vetting.
Fund management company proposing the investment change.
Fund’s home regulator, whose jurisdiction supplies the applicable home requirements.
objects: SFC-authorised fund and its domicile and UCITS classification.
Proposed material investment change, with objective, policy and restriction components identified separately.
Product features implicated by that change.
Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements.
Possible Hong Kong policy implications of the change.
Related SFC application, its receipt date and its approval or authorisation status at transition.
Revised scheme documents subject to filing and post-vetting.
left_frame.temporal_basis: Assess reliance on or after 28 November 2025, while separately fixing related application receipt and approval or authorisation status at the effective-date transition.
left_frame.unit_of_assessment: One identified material post-authorisation investment change for one fund, including its implicated product features and related application history.

assumptions: The expressions use Boolean operators and integer equality. For either flag integer, bit 0 is true exactly when the integer is odd; bit 1 is true exactly when the integer is 2 or 3.

fund_class_flags and change_scope_flags each have values only in 0, 1, 2 or 3. The European and UK classifications are separately recoverable; their mutual exclusivity follows only if the fund-specific domicile and authorisation premises are established.
The assessment date is a Gregorian calendar date, with the same value in both frames.
The home-requirement, feature, local-policy and application-history facts concern the identified change, not an unrelated feature or application.

For either model, true means eligibility for the stated removal within its scope. TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT labels that narrow true outcome only; it does not assert general legal compliance, approval or exemption from post-vetting.
The quoted circular and this model proposal do not establish the factual premises, the referenced FAQs' full requirements, or legal equivalence of the two formalizations.
